subject.title: [security] Public artifact URLs disclose authenticated owner and organization identities

question: Which stable secret and versioning policy should define non-reversible identity segments for future artifact grants while preserving existing v2 URLs?
rationale: This choice establishes both a cryptographic key-lifecycle contract and a persisted storage compatibility boundary that automation should not invent.

options.title: Domain-separated existing secret
options.body: Derive v3 organization and owner pseudonyms from an existing stable deployment secret with domain separation while leaving all v2 URLs valid.

options.title: Dedicated namespace secret
options.body: Add a separate versioned artifact-namespace secret with explicit setup, rotation, and migration documentation.

options.title: Accept documented disclosure
options.body: Retain reversible v2 segments and explicitly document that public artifact links expose exact authenticated identity metadata.

recommendation.title: Domain-separated existing secret
recommendation.body: Derive v3 organization and owner pseudonyms from an existing stable deployment secret with domain separation while leaving all v2 URLs valid.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the artifact key contract and the prior compatibility decision for new-write-only namespace changes.
